newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bayer plans 1.5 bln DM Asian investments.
newsitem.headline: Bayer plans 1.5 bln DM Asian investments.

text.p: Betting on strong growth in the Asian region, German chemicals and drugs group Bayer AG said on Tuesday it planned to invest at least 1.5 billion marks in the region to boost its global position.
"We will be spending more than 1.5 billion marks to expand our market position in Asia over the next four to five years," Bayer management board chairman Manfred Schneider told a news conference.
The group will focus largely on expanding its polymers business, Schneider added.
In Thailand Bayer acquired a company producing ABS plastics and plans to build a plant to produce Makrolon polycarbonate which is scheduled to come on stream in 1999.
Similarly Schneider said the group was taking a stake in a plastics group in India and had already embarked on capital expenditure programmes in Indonesia and Singapore and joint-ventures in China.

In the first nine months of 1996, the Asia/Africa/Australia region posted a 1.2 percent increase in sales totalling 4.2 billion marks. The group posted total sales of 36.54 billion marks in the same time.
Schneider explained that a relatively weak yen, as compared with the mark, had helped keep sales at lower levels. "In local currencies, sales rose by seven percent," he added.
